## 4. The more consequential extension: a whole-register strong converse

Now consider an arbitrary unknown \(n\)-qubit register, possibly globally entangled with an inaccessible reference.

Each bare source qubit suffers independent hidden noise \(\lambda\mathcal D[Z_j]\), and all noncommuting source interactions—including collective ones—obey

\[
\|[H(t),Z_j]\|\le\Omega
\quad\text{for every }j.
\]

The receiver can perform arbitrary **global** decoding. The actual acquired output is not assumed to factor into independent channels.

For any uniform success guarantee \(p>0\),

\[
\boxed{
F_{\mathrm{Bell}\mid\checkmark}
\le
\min\!\left\{
1,\,
\frac{C}{n}
+
\frac{\Omega}{\lambda p}
\frac{\ln n\,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil}{n}
\right\},
\qquad
C=e^{2/\mathrm e^2}<1.312.
}
\]

Therefore, at fixed \(\Omega/\lambda\) and nonvanishing success,

\[
\boxed{
F_{\mathrm{Bell}\mid\checkmark}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }n\longrightarrow\infty.
}
\]

For the Bell input, conditional trace-distance error is at least \(1-F\), so it tends to one.

This is uniform over acquisition time, receiver size, coherent waiting and collective postselection. It establishes more than a fixed error floor: increasingly elaborate downstream collection cannot turn this family of unencoded interfaces into a reliable importer of arbitrary growing quantum registers.

The logarithmic factors and the optimal register success-probability exponent are **not** claimed sharp.

### A resource comparison with ordinary transfer

A separate high-fidelity bound gives the necessary condition

\[
\boxed{
\frac{\Omega}{\lambda}
\ge
n\left[
\frac{p(1-2\epsilon)}{4\epsilon}-1
\right]
}
\]

for \(\epsilon\le1/4\), whenever the right side is positive.

At deterministic success, this requires \(\Omega/\lambda=\Omega(n/\epsilon)\).

Ordinary parallel SWAP transfer attains the same dependence up to constants when exchange access is available. With per-link Hamiltonian

\[
H_j=\frac{\Omega}{2}\operatorname{SWAP}_{S_jB_j},
\]

the transfer time is \(\pi/\Omega\), and

\[
\frac12\|\mathcal T-\mathrm{id}\|_\diamond
\le
1-e^{-\pi n\lambda/\Omega}
\le
\frac{\pi n\lambda}{\Omega}.
\]

A smooth \(\sin^2\) envelope doubles the time to \(2\pi/\Omega\) and has finite slew. It uses \(n\) receiving qubits and \(n\) parallel exchange interactions; aggregate peak interaction norm is \(n\Omega/2\).
